gloss: to give back-channel responses; to nod along

definitions.gloss: to give back-channel responses; to nod along; to make listening noises
definitions.explanation: To show the speaker that you are listening by interjecting short responses such as うん, はい, なるほど, そうですね, etc. An essential part of Japanese conversational etiquette.

examples.japanese: ⟦{話|はなし}→話：01496_hanashi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{聞|き}き→聞く：00483_kiku⟧⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧{相槌|あいづち}を{打|う}つ。
examples.english: To nod along while listening to someone talk.

examples.japanese: ⟦{上手|じょうず}→上手：00707_jouzu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{相槌|あいづち}→相槌：10916_aizuchi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{打|う}てる→打つ：01221_utsu⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{話|はな}し→話す：00467_hanasu⟧やすい。
examples.english: People who are good at giving back-channel responses are easy to talk to.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{会話|かいわ}→会話：01271_kaiwa⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{適度|てきど}→適度：03441_tekido⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{相槌|あいづち}を{打|う}つこと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦とても→とても：00593_totemo⟧⟦{大切|たいせつ}→大切：01456_taisetsu⟧だ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われている→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: In Japanese conversation, it is said to be very important to give back-channel responses at appropriate intervals.

notes:
USAGE:
Back-channeling (⟦{相槌|あいづち}→相槌：10916_aizuchi⟧) is a critical part of Japanese communication. Failing to give ⟦{相槌|あいづち}→相槌：10916_aizuchi⟧ may make the speaker feel ignored or uncomfortable. Common ⟦{相槌|あいづち}→相槌：10916_aizuchi⟧ include: うん, ⟦ええ→ええ：02893_ee⟧, はい, そうです⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧, ⟦なるほど→なるほど：01278_naruhodo⟧, ⟦{本当|ほんとう}→本当：00779_hontou⟧です⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {相槌|あいづち}を{打|う}つ (give back-channel responses)
- ⟦{適度|てきど}→適度：03441_tekido⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{相槌|あいづち}を{打|う}つ (give responses at appropriate intervals)
- ⟦{上手|じょうず}→上手：00707_jouzu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{相槌|あいづち}を{打|う}つ (give good back-channel responses)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Japanese speakers use ⟦{相槌|あいづち}→相槌：10916_aizuchi⟧ far more frequently than speakers of most other languages. This can be surprising for non-Japanese speakers, who may interpret the frequent はい and うん as agreement rather than simply acknowledgment of listening.
